summary: Independent review of the expected-quiet-service declaration, which closes the follow-up I recorded when pinning #968: because the reconciler is permanently silent, the Tracebacks row read PARTIAL_N/A on every run forever, so a newly-silent oms or schwab-1m-v2 would look identical at the level anybody actually reads and the exit code would not change. This PR is a real fix rather than another relabel, and I established that by mutation rather than by inspection. unexpected_silent_services is appended to failures, so a silent service that has NOT been declared quiet now fails the Tracebacks row and exits 1; removing that append turns a test RED, which is exactly the mutation that stayed green in #968 and is the difference between the two changes. codex-2 also added a guard I did not ask for: declaring a service quiet that was not also declared restarted raises EvidenceUnknown, so a typo'd or over-broad declaration cannot silently do nothing. Mutation matrix, 5 mutations against a baseline of 40 green, all RED: removing the failures append for undeclared silence (1); treating every silent service as expected-quiet (1); inverting the membership test so declared-quiet fails and undeclared passes (2); dropping the quiet-declaration-must-be-restarted guard (1); and removing unexpected_silent_services from the status expression so it labels without failing (1). REAL-BOX PROOF, read-only from /tmp with the deployment untouched at d87d8d1b, clean tree, temp files removed afterwards. I ran the head version BOTH ways to prove the operational consequence rather than assert it. Without --expected-quiet-service reconciler: reconciler=UNMEASURED(0/0), Tracebacks FAIL, Overall FAIL with 3 failed checks. With the flag: reconciler=N/A_EXPECTED_QUIET(0/0), Overall FAIL with 2 failed checks, the two being REST warmup and BOOT-HOLD which are Monday-dependent because Sunday has no scanner watchlist. oms reads 0/21564 and schwab-1m-v2 0/24775 timestamped records, so the two trading-relevant services carry genuine denominators. Controlled pair, full unit suite, sorted failure-NAME sets: base d87d8d1b 46 failed / 3776 passed, head 74a97b57 46 failed / 3779 passed, identical 46 names, zero new failures, and the +3 delta is exactly the three new tests, so the numbers reconcile without residue. The base matches #968's head, as it should. Both worktrees were asserted to import their own project_mai_tai before any count was trusted. Base is an ancestor of head; the diff is confined to the tool and its test file. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, which the post-merge sequence must respect: syncing the checkout to the merged SHA WITHOUT adding --expected-quiet-service reconciler to the evidence call turns the reconciler into UNMEASURED and FAILS the gate. That is now proven on the box, not inferred. Code and flag must land in the SAME action, alongside the EXPECTED_SHA update, and the sync must not restart any service; EXPECTED_PID 1089323 and EXPECTED_START 2026-09-12 20:34:27 UTC remain correct. RESIDUAL RISK, recorded and not blocking, because it is a process exposure rather than a code defect: the quiet declaration lives in preopen.sh on the box, which is edited outside the review-pin gate. Someone can quiet a genuinely broken service by adding a flag there, and nothing in this repo would catch it. If that matters later, the declaration belongs in a reviewed file rather than in a hand-edited shell script on the host. CI: validate to be confirmed before I use the word pinned.
